title: Cell resolution (the three-tier ladder)
description: The single contract every resolution tier emits and passes up the escalation chain (run-population-redesign.md). EXTENDS the per-cell metadata of runtime-shapes.md §2 with the tier fields (resolved_by, hypothesis, attempts[]), a source row_id, and the NOT_LOCATED reason code. `cell` is the row in C1's `cells` table; `triage_decision` is the Tier-2 LLM's per-step output. The same `cell` shape is updated by all three tiers — Tier 1 (try_direct), Tier 2 (try_llm), Tier 3 (try_agent); each tier updates the cell IN PLACE in the run store, growing attempts[].

source.description: One source a cell value was drawn from — a list entry on a cell (a cell may draw from several databases/rows). The cohort identity is NOT repeated here: it is the cell's `member` (every source of a cell is, by construction, that member's). For a direct copy from a one-row-per-identity table, {database, query, table_column} is enough to re-extract the value. For a one-to-many table (e.g. clinical_notes) or an interpreted value, `row_id` (the evidence row's own primary key) pins the exact source row, and `citations` carries the verbatim passage(s) read from it.

query.description: The read-only SQL that produced the value, showing it ALONGSIDE its row identity (never a bare SELECT <value>; doc 6). Required.

table_column.description: The `table.column` the value came from. Required.

row_id.description: The evidence row's OWN primary key, recorded when the value comes from a one-to-many table (many notes per patient) or was interpreted — the cell's `member` identifies the patient but not which of their rows. Omit for a direct copy from a one-row-per-identity table.

citations.description: Verbatim passage(s) read from THIS source's row — EXACT word-for-word substrings so a highlight lands. Present only when `table_column` is free text (a clinical note); one note can yield several. Omit for a structured-column copy. This is where the old flat cell-level `evidence[]` now lives, linked to the exact row it came from.

attempt.description: ONE attempt to fill the cell's value, in resolution order. The first entry is the Tier-1 direct pass: the value it read (`value`) and where it read it (`table_column`, plus the narrowed `sql`), with `error` set when that value was not usable (NULL, off-code-map). A later entry is appended each time a higher tier tries to fill the cell — a triage retry (carries the `sql` the LLM ran and its `result`), or a proposed value that was rejected at write time (carries that `value` and the `error`, e.g. off-code). The cell's `hypothesis` is the reason the first LLM thinks the direct pass failed. `sql` is present only when a query was actually involved.

tier.description: Which tier made this attempt. Required.

database.description: Which database this attempt touched (the source db slug). Always present so a reader knows where the attempt looked; the sentinel "(none)" is used when no database was involved (e.g. an off-code rejection or the agent's NOT_LOCATED fallback). Required.

sql.description: The read-only SQL involved in this attempt (the narrowed Tier-1 query the value was read from, or the SQL a triage retry ran — validated by validate_sql before running). Optional: a pure value-fill attempt (e.g. a code-drift translation, or a write rejected before any query) carries none.

value.description: The value this attempt tried to place in the cell — the raw value the direct pass read (the one that then failed), or the value a higher tier proposed that was rejected at write time. Optional (absent when the source was simply NULL/empty).

table_column.description: The `table.column` this attempt's value was read from — written by Tier 1 from the executable's cell_map so higher tiers need not re-parse the SQL. Optional.

result.description: A short rendering of what a query returned (the value, a row count, or a sample). Optional — absent if the query errored or no query ran.

error.description: The error this attempt hit — a SQL error (column renamed) or a resolution error (value not in code_set / off-code at write time). Absent on a clean result. The first LLM to see a non-empty error writes the cell's `hypothesis`.

cell.description: One cell of the run store (C1's `cells` table). Inserted `pending` at run start with sheet/ref/field/member already set, then updated in place by the tiers. A blocked cell has no `value` but still carries `state` + the blocked-only fields.

sheet.description: The workbook sheet the cell is on. Required.

field.description: The audit field id this cell carries (matches spec.json's field identifier). Set at pending-insert time from the mapping's executable block; lets the agent and the FE pivot 'open cells for field X' without parsing ref. Required.

member.description: The cohort-member identity this cell carries (the patient/encounter code). Set at pending-insert time from the resolved cohort; lets the agent pivot 'open cells for member Y' and lets Tier-2/Tier-3 queries bind by member without re-parsing sources. Required.

kind.description: How the value is obtained (carried from mapping.json). Required.

state.description: The cell's lifecycle state — the SINGLE non-terminal value plus the three terminal ones (doc 5 §Cell state model). `pending` = inserted at run start, not yet resolved by the ladder (the 'open set' the next tier acts on); `filled`/`blocked`/`not_applicable` are terminal. A cell stays `pending` through every escalation until a tier settles it — there is NO separate 'error'/'open'/tier-ownership status, because which tier is currently on a cell is ephemeral orchestration state recoverable from `attempts[]`, not durable cell state. What was tried lives in `attempts[]`/`hypothesis`. Needs-verification is likewise NOT a state — it is DERIVED (filled + kind interpret + review_state not_reviewed) and never stored. "unknown" is NOT a state either — an agent that searched and could not place the value is `blocked` with reason_code NOT_LOCATED. Required.

value.description: The cell value, as a string. Present when state is filled; absent when blocked/not_applicable.

confidence.description: The WORD low/medium/high, never a number (drives the heat-map). Required.

resolved_by.description: Which tier produced the terminal result. Required. NEW vs runtime-shapes §2.

hypothesis.description: Best explanation for WHY the direct pass failed, written by the first LLM to examine the failure. null on a clean direct hit. NEW vs runtime-shapes §2.

attempts.description: Log of actual DB queries, in order; the escalation payload passed up the ladder. A clean direct hit is exactly one entry with no error. Required (non-empty). NEW vs runtime-shapes §2.

explanation.description: The ONE-sentence plain-language account of how the value was derived: for a direct copy, that it was copied from the source column; for an interpreted value, how the cited passages were combined to infer it. Present for resolved cells.

sources.description: One entry per (database, row) the value drew on — the value's full provenance, including any verbatim `citations` per source (the old flat `evidence[]` now lives inside each source). Present for filled cells.

corrected.description: interpret-only: did the user edit it after reviewing? Optional.

reason_code.description: blocked-only: why the value is absent. The doc-10 taxonomy PLUS NOT_LOCATED (the agent searched and could not place the value — attempts[] is the explanation). Required when state is blocked.

reason_detail.description: blocked-only: evidence-grade detail of exactly what is missing and where it was looked for. Required when state is blocked.

owner_needed.description: blocked-only: the role/specialty/source to chase. Optional.

outstanding_since.description: blocked-only: how long the gap has been open. Optional.

prompt_version.description: The prompt version that produced the cell (ties to the run record, doc 7). Optional.

allOf.description: A resolved (terminal) cell carries its provenance; a `pending` cell need not (it has not been settled yet).
A blocked cell declares why and how long.

triage_decision.description: The triage LLM's per-step output (Tier 2), BEFORE a terminal cell is produced. One polymorphic `output` disambiguated by `decision`. The LLM authors ONLY the interpretive part: for a solution it returns the value plus the verbatim `citations` it used and a one-sentence `explanation` of how it combined them — it never authors SQL or row identities; the tier grounds each citation to its source row and builds the cell's `sources[]`.

decision.description: solution = `output` is the cell value; retry = `output` is the next read-only SQL to run; escalate = hand to the agent (`output` null). Required.

output.description: The cell value (decision=solution), the next read-only SQL (decision=retry), or null (decision=escalate).

reason.description: Always present. For solution it becomes the cell's `hypothesis`; for retry it states why the query should work; for escalate it is a short note (the agent receives attempts[] regardless). Required.

citations.description: decision=solution only, and only when the value was interpreted from free text (a clinical note): the verbatim passage(s) the value was inferred from, copied EXACTLY (each must be a substring of a note returned by the evidence shown). The tier matches each citation back to its source row to build `sources[].citations`. Omit for a direct/structured solution.

explanation.description: decision=solution only: the one-sentence account of how the value was derived (how the citations were combined / which column it was read from). Becomes the cell's `explanation`. Omit for retry/escalate.

source_column.description: decision=solution AND the value is a STRUCTURED (non-note) read — the `table.column` the value came from (e.g. "charts.value"). Use this instead of `citations` when the value is not from free-text: the tier records it as the source's table_column. Omit for a note-derived solution (use citations), and for retry/escalate.

allOf.description: solution and retry must carry a non-null output; escalate must not.
Only a solution may carry citations/explanation/source_column.
